#### Surviving a bug fix — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** The two assumptions Kappa rests on, made into checks rather than hopes.

`replayThrough` is the architecture's only recovery mechanism, and it works: 45 from 9 retained events through the fixed pipeline.

`verify` then names what that result depends on. Step 2: 6 retained events give 30 — a confident wrong answer with no error. Step 3: a non-deterministic pipeline gives 45, the **right** total with `trustworthy` false. The totals alone cannot tell you which replay to believe.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

All 9 retained events through the fixed pipeline: `total` = 45. This is the architecture working — one codebase, one replay, the right answer. The two steps that follow are the assumptions this result quietly depends on.

<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — short retention produces a smaller total and no error</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch10-system-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: short retention produces a smaller total and no error" width="980">

With 6 of 9 events retained the replay returns 30 — a complete, confident, wrong answer. Only this explicit check distinguishes it from 45; the replay itself raises nothing. "We can always reprocess" is true exactly as far back as retention.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — and a non-deterministic pipeline gives the right total for the wrong reason</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch10-system-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: and a non-deterministic pipeline gives the right total for the wrong reason" width="980">

`loose` has `total` = 45 and `trustworthy` false — the number is right and the guarantee is not. A pipeline that reads the wall clock happens to agree on this replay and will not on the next, and no amount of log completeness fixes it: the pipeline has stopped being a function of its input.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — so two assumptions carry the whole architecture</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch10-system-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: so two assumptions carry the whole architecture" width="980">

Read the three heap rows: totals 45, 30 and 45, with `trustworthy` true, false and false. The totals alone cannot tell you which replay to believe — which is why retention length and determinism belong in a test rather than in an assumption.
